candidate_refinements.refinement: Narrow the claim-compiled regime-shift mechanism-fidelity gate. The released CAWM checker demonstrates that manually specified signed predictions plus manually chosen nearby regimes can falsify all four over-generalization CAWM cases in the released study, while three companion checks use a known-principled observable. It does not implement or validate autonomous parsing of an arbitrary novel mechanism claim into the signed prediction, nor autonomous selection of the falsifying regime.
candidate_refinements.scope_guard: The published 7/7 checks were constructed after episode coding, so 7/7 is an in-sample post-hoc consistency result, not a prospective detection rate or evidence that an in-loop gate improves scientific discovery.

candidate_refinements.refinement: Verification-first catalysis literature independently specifies typed claims, evidence admissibility, verifier-triggered additional calculations/sensitivity tests/experiments, and downgrade/prune on conflict, but the 2026 npj Artificial Intelligence article is a Perspective/design argument, not a matched efficacy ablation. Treat it as architectural convergence, not causal performance evidence.

negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: The public CAWM checker hard-codes episode-specific claim-to-prediction mappings, regimes and thresholds; automatic claim compilation and regime selection remain an unverified research problem.
Three of seven CAWM detections are companion recomputations that presuppose a principled observable; they do not establish verification when the correct mechanism/observable is unknown.

The CAWM paper explicitly frames self-application of the regime-shift check before reporting as a next experiment, confirming that the released result is post-hoc detection rather than an already tested in-loop intervention.

A 2026 autonomous-research-agent verification-gap survey reports that under its coding rule none of nine closed-loop L4 systems demonstrated an externally validated in-loop oracle; this is corpus-level secondary evidence for the verification gap, not an intervention effect.

A small public sci-agent-verification-cascade fixture reports deterministic source-ID checks causing corrections while a model-based semantic checker caused none, but all actions were already correct, so it cannot establish downstream scientific-quality improvement.
